PullRequest.Title: Git - 💄 better error handling and clean-up logging

Scenarios.Scenario: Git extension activation, including missing Git and model-creation failures
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Activation awaits findGit and IPC-server creation before constructing the model and registering Git services. Initial repository scanning is started by the model constructor but is not awaited by createModel. Missing-Git repository checks and the warning prompt are also not awaited by activation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate Git executables with --version and platform discovery commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Sequentially try H hints until success, followed on failure by platform-specific fallback candidates. macOS additionally uses which and possibly xcode-select.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical candidate order, command count, and awaiting; the diff only prefixes existing discovery messages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Executable discovery must finish before model creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the local HTTP IPC server and listen on its pipe/socket for Git helpers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One server creation attempt per createModel call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same server creation and error recovery; only the failure-log text changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: createModel awaits the creation attempt, as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Unlink a stale Unix socket; on missing Git, stat each file-scheme workspace folder's .git entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one socket unlink per server creation; W parallel stat checks only on the missing-Git warning path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Socket setup is awaited. Missing-Git stat checks run in the unawaited warning task.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Format and enqueue activation-failure log messages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One warning and console message per caught model-creation failure, newly including failures other than missing Git.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Missing-Git failures already logged; other creation failures were rethrown without this warning. The additional work is bounded per failed activation, not per discovered file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Formatting occurs in the catch; output-channel delivery is scheduled through channelPromise.then and is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured Git path hints H, platform fallback candidates, and workspace folders W for the missing-Git check.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Git candidates are tried sequentially. Missing-Git stat checks use Promise.all. IPC creation remains one attempt.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new discovery cache or retry loop. Existing hint/fallback behavior is unchanged; logger channel initialization remains shared through its promise.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: activation and helper implementations establish unchanged expensive-boundary counts and scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timing measurements; platform discovery latency and workspace-folder counts vary. The only new failure work is a bounded diagnostic message.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: no additional discovery, IPC setup, or repository checks, and bounded failure logging does not establish a realistic degradation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial multi-root repository discovery and first SCM status
Scenarios.CriticalPath: doInitialScan awaits workspace-root detection, visible-editor detection, and subfolder scanning before setting initialized through finally. Each repository open awaits root resolution and repository construction, publishes it to SCM, then starts status without awaiting it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read directory entries and resolve candidate, repository, and workspace real paths; check HEAD synchronously in untrusted workspaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One readdir per visited directory. Non-exact-open candidate lookups can perform realpath before root resolution and again for the resolved root. Successful workspace realpaths are cached by folder path; failed resolutions can retry. All counts are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical traversal depth, ignored-folder filtering, path deduplication, realpath cache, and HEAD check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Traversal and candidate resolution are awaited by the initial scan; repository realpath runs alongside dotGit discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve repository roots and Git directories using rev-parse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Candidates not already matched by an exact open repository run root discovery, usually one rev-parse with an additional command in the symbolic-link case. Each newly opened repository performs one combined --git-dir/--git-common-dir command. Untrusted bare-repository checks can add the existing --show-cdup call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same subprocess counts, guards, root deduplication, and global per-model sequentialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These commands are awaited before opening that repository; openRepository is serialized across the entire Model instance.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Populate HEAD, remotes, submodules, and working-tree status using existing Git commands and metadata reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing initial status per newly opened repository, coalesced by the per-repository throttle. Metadata requests run in Promise.all before getStatus.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical status scheduling and metadata/status work; the new opened-repository diagnostic replaces the old info-level open diagnostic, which is now trace-level.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Started without awaiting after the repository has been announced to SCM; can overlap later repository opens.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create SCM providers/resource groups, update command contexts, and publish status resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider per new repository and existing context/resource updates; no added per-file or per-repository IPC beyond logging.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider registration occurs during construction/open; status-resource publication follows asynchronous status.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform configured background fetch through existing repository fetch methods.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing loop per eligible trusted repository when autofetch is enabled; waits for idle/focus and the configured period between fetches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same enablement, loop ownership, and scheduling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background work, not awaited by model initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue scan start/completion/settings diagnostics and format collection counts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two new info messages and one settings trace per initial scan; completion computes array-backed lengths once, O(R plus closed/parent/unsafe counts). Successful opens retain one info diagnostic each, with the old location changed to trace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No scan start/completion diagnostics. Collection-wide scan-path formatting already existed and remains unchanged. The successful-open info message is relocated rather than duplicated at info level.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Count formatting occurs once before scan completion. Log delivery is not awaited; a visible output channel can flush/update through its existing path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace roots W; readable directories D within configured scan depth; unique candidate paths C per workspace after Set deduplication; successfully opened repository roots R. Different candidate subfolders may still resolve to the same repository, as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Three initial discovery branches and workspace-folder traversals use Promise.all. Traversal within a workspace is sequential. All openRepository calls share one sequentialize queue per Model, not one queue per path. Status is throttled per repository and may overlap across repositories.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Open repositories avoid exact duplicate opens. Candidate sets deduplicate paths within each workspace scan; workspace realpaths cache successful resolutions but not failures. Closed, parent, and unsafe repository managers retain their existing sets/maps. No cache invalidation or coalescing change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: complete changed hunks, sequentialize/throttle implementations, discovery helpers, and status call path confirm unchanged costly work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large/deep workspaces and slow filesystems can make the existing scan expensive, but no measured latency is available. The added count-array allocation is once per scan, not per candidate, and does not establish a material regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded diagnostics and catches without increasing discovery cardinality, process concurrency, or awaited status work. Existing fan-out and negative-cache behavior are not introduced by this PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Runtime editor switches, workspace/configuration changes, filesystem discovery, and repository closure
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor-change and workspace-change handlers await their existing candidate opens, but do not gate editor display. Configuration and debounced filesystem handlers enqueue opens without awaiting. Repository closure synchronously disposes its owned listeners/watchers/SCM resources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use the existing repository-open path's realpath and Git discovery operations for unresolved candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Editors already covered by an open repository skip discovery. Added/config-enabled roots skip existing repositories. Filesystem events deduplicate paths in a Set for 500 ms; queued opens remain globally serialized per Model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same candidate filters, debounce, deduplication, queue, and boundary calls; added try/catch only logs failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Async event handlers await opens where they already did; filesystem/configuration events do not await. No new awaited boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register or dispose existing SCM resources and update repository/context state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per actual open/close; removal preserves repositories still required by visible editors or remaining workspace folders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical ownership, disposal ordering, manager updates, and subscriptions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing disposal runs before added-folder opens; explicit close records the closed repository and disposes it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Format existing trace/info messages and new caught-error warnings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-editor/per-event diagnostics are renamed; one unconditional editor-scan trace is removed. New warnings occur once per failed handler invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing diagnostic frequency is preserved or reduced on successful events. Failed handlers previously propagated their errors without the new warning.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Output delivery remains unawaited through the log-channel promise.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible editors E, added/removed workspace folders W, existing repositories R, and unique possible-repository paths collected over each 500 ms debounce window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Promise.all submits editor/folder candidates, but one Model-wide queue executes opens serially. Filesystem events coalesce for 500 ms. Repository status remains independently throttled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Same open-repository lookups, successful workspace-realpath cache, no negative candidate cache, and transient possibleGitRepositoryPaths Set cleared after each debounce flush. No new retained collection or lost cleanup handle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: handlers, watcher wiring, queue/debounce decorators, and disposal closures are unchanged apart from logging and catch wrappers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Event rates and repository counts vary; repeated failed non-repository probes are pre-existing. No evidence that catch logging causes a realistic resource problem.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix. The removed inexpensive trace alone does not establish a prior performance symptom.

Scenarios.Scenario: Clone a repository through a Git URI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The URI handler parses and validates the URI, awaits command availability, then dispatches git.clone. The clone command awaits destination selection and the clone subprocess before offering to open the result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query commands, dispatch git.clone, show the destination picker/progress, and optionally open the cloned repository or download link.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getCommands query and one clone dispatch per valid URI with Git available; existing user prompts and post-clone action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same validation, commands query, dispatch, and prompts; only diagnostic prefixes change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Availability and destination selection precede cloning. URI handler does not await executeCommand, as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check destination-name existence and create the parent directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Sequential existence checks bounded by count < 20, followed by existing mkdirp.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical filesystem checks and directory setup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute git clone with progress and optional branch selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One clone subprocess per accepted URI request; no additional subprocess introduced by the logging change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same subprocess arguments, cancellation, progress parsing, and awaiting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Clone command awaits process completion before post-clone actions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transfer the requested repository through the Git subprocess for remote URLs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing clone transfer per request, scaling with repository contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same remote URL and transfer behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Transfer must finish before the cloned repository can be opened.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One clone request/URL per handled URI, repository transfer size, and up to 19 existing destination-name checks before choosing the final candidate.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each request follows its existing independent async flow. The diff introduces neither batching changes nor additional parallel clone operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache. Command availability is queried per valid request as before; URL serialization already existed in the same log locations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all URI-handler hunks only add log prefixes; the command and Git implementations confirm unchanged boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Clone duration depends on network and repository size, but there is no changed mechanism affecting either.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: existing URI serialization, filesystem checks, command IPC, and network/subprocess work are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all three changed files and every diff page for base e852c335aac2aab40baf3931c391668f2dd1b202 to head aacb1b878b87298d9327999946e8d2f9def6e8c8. Traced startup, initial/runtime discovery, cleanup, output logging, and URI cloning, including effective concurrency and positive/negative cache behavior. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete regression fix established. Static read-only review; no performance measurements.
